cells.quote: Finally, — and this emerges from the above — collaboration has changed scale. The foundational situation of collaborative learning is, historically, that of the small group (or even the dyad), where students work together in a largely synchronous manner in the classroom. And what might be termed the classical definition of collaboration was predicated on that situation (Roschelle & Teasley, 1995; Dillenbourg, 1999; Baker, 2015), in that it involves mostly synchronous agency towards a shared representation of a problem, over a limited timescale.
